agent_authored.description: DScribe 2.1.2 is a Python/C++ library that transforms atomistic structures into numerical descriptors for materials modelling and machine learning. This source-only registration proposes one combined descriptor environment covering SOAP, MBTR/LMBTR/Valle-Oganov, ACSF, and Coulomb/Sine/Ewald matrices.

shared_components.title: Descriptor, geometry, parallel, binding, build, and Eigen support
shared_components.purpose: Provides descriptor base classes, atomic-system conversion, parallel execution, geometry and neighbour-list utilities, the pybind11 bridge, common C++ descriptor classes, weighting functions, Eigen headers, and extension build configuration.
shared_components.relationship: All descriptor families are compiled into one extension and reuse the same Python hierarchy, atomic-system conversion, neighbour geometry, parallel driver, and Eigen/build infrastructure; it is accounted once rather than repeated per former family.

modules.title: Combined atomistic descriptors and derivatives
modules.expensive_path: Neighbour enumeration feeds SOAP basis contractions, MBTR/LMBTR pair and triplet histogram accumulation, ACSF radial/angular sums, and dense or Ewald matrix construction; analytical or finite-difference derivatives multiply these workloads, while all families share the same compiled extension, geometry, parallel, and build stack.
modules.rationale: The four descriptor families expose different representations but form one coherent DScribe descriptor subsystem. Their owned numerical kernels total 11,636 source-like physical lines, while separating them would duplicate a much larger 1,859-file/400,691-line support stack and leave three thin environments. One environment preserves meaningful breadth and one build/runtime contract.
excluded: dscribe.kernels similarity aggregation, whose sparse official coverage and downstream aggregation role do not justify a second environment
documentation, plotting, and machine-learning training examples, which are downstream demonstrations rather than owned numerical kernels
hazards: Feature indices are physical only for a fixed descriptor configuration; sparse storage order is not.
Periodic image enumeration and large reductions may change floating-point summation order across targets.
Random matrix permutation must be graded statistically or with controlled seeds, never by raw draw order.
Eigenspectra compare ordered eigenvalues, not eigenvector signs or phases.
Analytical and numerical derivatives have different attainable numerical floors.
modules.purpose: Computes local and global atomistic representations and their supported coordinate derivatives: SOAP density-overlap spectra, MBTR-family geometry histograms, Behler-Parrinello ACSF, and Coulomb/Sine/Ewald matrices.
primary_inputs: periodic cells and accuracy/cutoff settings where applicable
primary_outputs: dense NumPy or sparse COO descriptor arrays
algorithm_stages: convert atomic systems and enumerate neighbours/images
evaluate family-specific basis, histogram, symmetry-function, or pair-interaction kernels
optionally evaluate analytical or numerical derivatives
modules.differences: The families differ in representation and dominant kernel, but jointly constitute the public descriptor subsystem and share a larger common compiled/runtime foundation than any thin family owns alone.

official_tests.summary: A native editable build with GCC/G++ 12.2 and Python 3.12 collected and passed 415 items. The combined descriptor-owned suites account for 395 collected items; each former family completed in under one minute. ASE 3.26.0 was used for compatibility with the pinned System.from_atoms implementation.
